node.name: Sunday Trivia Nights at Bobbi’s
node.descriptionText:
Trivia at Bobbi’s runs about 90 minutes and is played over five rounds. The game features a slideshow format with image-based and puzzle categories, making it engaging, easy to follow, and accessible for players with hearing difficulties.

Questions span history, science, music, film, television, geography, and more, creating a well-rounded game that appeals to players of all experience levels and interests.

A strong emphasis is placed on teamwork, with categories designed to encourage group thinking and collaboration. Bobbi’s puzzle rounds are especially popular, known for their creativity and memorable “A-ha!” moments.

Trivia at Bobbi’s is always free to play, with prizes and bragging rights for the top-scoring teams. All are welcome!

node.name: Dispelling Fear
node.foodDetails: Tea & Mochi Social Hour follows at 8pm!
node.descriptionText: Fear is a state of heart and mind that is disabling, demotivating, and corrosive. Freeing ourselves from the grip of fear is key to flourishing, intimacy, and awakening. This Sunday, we will look at the nature of fear, describe its qualities, and envision what fearlessness looks like. We will practice a marvelous meditation for dissolving fear, as developed by Tara Brach. (The Abhaya Mudra, or hand gesture of fearlessness, depicted above, is used to dispel fear and calm the mind.)

node.name: Volunteer with Sunrise Cafe!
node.descriptionText:
Start your morning off on a great note! Join Dwight Hall Monday and Wednesday mornings to volunteer at Sunrise Cafe. Sunrise Cafe is an early morning soup kitchen that serves New Haven's homeless and food-insecure every weekday from 6:30 A.M. to 8:30 A.M. The service site is located at 57 Olive St., just a 15 minute walk from Phelps Gate. Volunteers will meet in front of Phelps Gate at 6:00am, walk together to Sunrise Cafe, and will return to campus by 9:00am.

To sign up, please request to join DWIGHT HALL VOLUNTEER CORPS, and we will approve your request as soon as possible.

Sunrise Cafe has been serving breakfast without charge to New Haven's homeless and hungry since 2015. Each weekday morning, the Cafe welcomes guests to the undercroft of St. Paul and St. James, near Wooster Square and three blocks south of the New Haven Green with white tablecloths, flowers and a rotating menu of fresh, warm, nutritious home-cooked food. Your generosity opens our doors.

Cheerful volunteers take each order individually, deliver the breakfast to our guest and help our paid chefs in the kitchen. Staff and volunteers ensure every guest is warmly welcomed.

Sunrise Cafe is uniquely welcoming and secure, based on trust and mutual respect, and the rapport built between the volunteer servers and our guests. With a warm welcome and just two rules – no drugs on the premises and no arguments – Sunrise has become a community center for the homeless, a place to come every weekday morning and gather with friends.

Hungry friends come for the home-cooked, nourishing breakfast and stay for simple medical services offered by the Cornell Scott Health Center and access to support from social services to find housing.

Sunrise provides a unique opportunity to bridge New Haven's inequalities that separate us from one another. Volunteers come once and become regulars. Guests and volunteers become friends and greet one another on the street.

If you have any questions, email maryann.dang@yale.edu

node.name: How to Cite and Report AI Use
node.descriptionText: Interested in writing about your research—scholarly, public, policy, and more—and working with AI? Join us to learn more about how to transparently describe your work! This discipline-agnostic workshop is interested in helping you make better decisions around how to communicate your AI use, whether you are machine translating primary texts for a humanities dissertation, or using AI/machine learning to analyze health data in a journal article, or using AI for writing assistance. We’ll refer to guidelines from journals, professional associations, and disciplinary communities.
node.descriptionHtml:
Interested in writing about your research—scholarly, public, policy, and more—and working with AI? Join us to learn more about how to transparently describe your work! 

This discipline-agnostic workshop is interested in helping you make better decisions around how to communicate your AI use, whether you are machine translating primary texts for a humanities dissertation, or using AI/machine learning to analyze health data in a journal article, or using AI for writing assistance. We’ll refer to guidelines from journals, professional associations, and disciplinary communities.  

Participants will leave able to... 

  • Construct AI use statements to describe their use of AI tools in both conducting studies and writing, with reference to established recommendations and best practices  
  • Identify and use relevant data and software citation practices, professional body recommendations, and reporting guidelines relevant to using, citing, and reporting AI   
  • Recognize and mitigate potential threats to the accuracy of your citations

node.name: Daily Worship at Marquand Chapel
node.descriptionText:
Join us at 11:30am in Marquand Chapel for our daily worship.

Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worship. So Marquand is also actively engaged in original, creative, and experimental forms of worship, both for committed Christians and for those exploring the faith.

node.name: Investing 101, Financial Life After Yale – Investing and Taxes
node.descriptionText:
A simple yet powerful tool in accumulating your wealth and investing has many components of it. To successfully get the most out of your investments, it’s important to first learn the basics. On top of that, it’s important to understand how taxes work. In this session, learn how you can start investing and why it’s crucial to start as soon as possible and stay on the course. node.name: Monday Mindfulness Meditation
node.descriptionText:
Free afternoon group meditation held on Zoom sponsored by Being Well at Yale (Employee Well-being).  Sessions are held during the academic year September through mid-December and mid-January through end of May. 

Taking a break during the workday to pause and practice mindfulness has been shown to be beneficial for enhancing executive function, increasing emotional regulation, and reducing cortisol levels. Meditations are a mix of guided and silent. Time for reflections and optional sharing is also included at the conclusion of the practice. 

Beginners welcome! No experience necessary. No special equipment required. Open to Yale University employees. 

Sessions are led by Danielle Casioppo, Education Specialist and Certified Mindfulness-Based Strengths Practice instructor with Being Well at Yale / Employee Well-being. 

To join please send a request to beingwell@yale.edu and specify your Yale affiliation. You will then be added to the Yale meditation email list serve. The Zoom link to join the sessions is included in the weekly reminder emails.

node.name: SustyVibes US Launch and Film Screening of The Eco-Anxiety Africa Project
node.descriptionText:
Join us for the official launch of SustyVibes United States, marking the start of a new youth-led movement connecting climate action and mental wellbeing across America.

The evening will open with a screening of The Eco-Anxiety Africa Project (TEAP), a documentary revealing how our changing climate is shaping the mental wellbeing of young people across Africa.

Following the screening, stay for a fireside panel — Eco-Anxiety in the Polycrisis: Support and Safeguarding for Young People's Mental Health in the US — bringing together experts working at the intersection of climate change, mental health, and youth development.

This conversation will connect lived experience to action, offering practical insight into building youth-centred climate resilience in your own community. We'll also unveil our founding cohort of US-based SustyVibers, who will lead on climate resilience initiatives over the next 18 months. Perfect for anyone interested in climate advocacy, youth mental health, and community-centred sustainability work.

This launch event is hosted in collaboration with The Planetary Health Alliance.
If you'd like to apply to become one of our pioneer sustyvibers, apply via https://bit.ly/JoinSustyVibesUS

node.name: A conversation with Yale Law School Professor John Morley '06
node.descriptionText:
Join us for a conversation with Yale Law School Professor John Morley '06 as he discusses his remarkable career and the business of Big Law. 

John Morley is Augustus E. Lines Professor of Law at Yale Law School and a theorist of organization. He studies how the law encourages — and discourages — cooperation. His research has probed the foundations of a wide variety of businesses and social groups, including ordinary corporations, investment funds, trusts, law firms, customer cooperatives, mutual financial institutions, marriages, cities, states, and nations. 

Morley is active in shaping real-world organizations. He was the primary drafter of the Anthropic Long-Term Benefit Trust agreement and has served since the Trust’s founding in 2023 as its principal legal counsel. He regularly advises major companies and institutions on challenging problems in governance, including public benefit mission commitments, mutual ownership governance, and AI safety. He has testified as an expert witness in proceedings related to trusts, investment funds, and general corporate organization.

Morley has a special interest in the regulation and structure of investment funds. He has authored many articles on hedge funds, mutual funds, and private equity funds. He also has a focus on the law of trusts and estates. He served as the reporter for the Uniform Directed Trust Act, which has now been adopted by the legislatures of 22 states. 

Morley also writes and speaks frequently about the governance of law firms. With Joel Cohen, he co-hosts New Law Order, a popular podcast on the legal profession.

He received undergraduate degrees in political science and economics from the University of Utah and his law degree from Yale Law School.
